title: How Does Autocorrect Know What You Meant?
sources: Dictionary.com, 'How Does Autocorrect Ducking Work, Anyway?' (2013): autocorrect began as a smart spellchecker relying on a dictionary ('bfeore' -> 'before'); smartphone autocorrect suggests words that contain letters near the letters in the misspelled word; Microsoft's 2007 'contextual speller' uses the surrounding words ('shew ent' -> 'she went'); Cupertino appeared in documents published by the UN, NATO and other official bodies

Oxford University Press blog, Ben Zimmer, 'Spellchecker' (Nov 2007): older spellcheckers had wordlists containing 'co-operation' but not 'cooperation' without the hyphen, and suggested 'Cupertino', a city in northern California; dozens of Cupertinos in documents from the UN, EU, NATO and other international organizations

kottke.org (Nov 2006), 'The Cupertino effect': term for incorrect spellcheck suggestions that make it into finalized documents, named for its appearance in European Union documents in place of 'cooperation'

lines.text: How does autocorrect know what you meant to type?
lines.caps: HOW DOES *AUTOCORRECT | KNOW WHAT YOU *MEANT | TO *TYPE?

lines.text: Well, every word you type gets checked against a dictionary,
lines.caps: WELL *EVERY WORD | YOU *TYPE | GETS *CHECKED | AGAINST A *DICTIONARY

lines.text: and if it's not there, the phone hunts for the closest real word.
lines.caps: AND IF IT'S *NOT | *THERE | THE PHONE *HUNTS | FOR THE *CLOSEST | REAL *WORD

lines.text: It knows which keys sit next to each other,
so if your thumb slips onto a neighbor, it spots the mistake.
lines.caps: SO IF YOUR *THUMB | *SLIPS ONTO | A *NEIGHBOR | IT *SPOTS | THE *MISTAKE

lines.text: Then it looks at the words around it,
and picks the one that fits the sentence best.
Old spell checkers only knew cooperation with a hyphen,
so when people typed it without one,
the top suggestion was Cupertino, a city in California,
and it slipped into real United Nations and EU documents.
So autocorrect isn't reading your mind, it's playing the odds.
